title: Forgetting module coefficients in the stalk of derived exchange
statement: Let Λ be any commutative ring, X prime → X, X → Y and X prime → Y prime a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], t: Spec Ω → Y prime with Ω separably closed [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], F a sheaf of Λ-modules on X [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and q ≥ 0. Write G=F_ab [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. There exist additive equivalences b1 and b2 from the underlying groups of the source and target stalks of the module baseChangeHomologyMap to the corresponding stalks of H^q(g^* Rf_* G[0]) and H^q(Rf prime_* g prime^* G[0]), such that b2 Ex_module = Ex_abelian b1, where Ex_abelian is degree-q homology of derivedBaseChangeMapPlus [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. There is no strict-local, compactness, properness or torsion hypothesis, and no total-space cohomology group occurs.

source.place: Tag 03FD and proof (acyclic module/abelian comparison); Tag 0736 and Remark 07A7 (termwise mate). The compatibility of these comparisons is expanded by worker J1.

proof.text: Use the canonical exact coefficient forgetful functors and the derived direct-image comparison. The proved underived inverse-image isomorphism lifts to D⁺. Compose these edge comparisons to get the source and target derived isomorphisms for F[0], and use mapDerivedCategoryPlusSingleFunctor to identify the forgotten single complex with the abelian one.

Apply moduleAbelianDerivedExchange_compatibility to F[0]. Naturality of abelian derived exchange transports this equality through the single-functor comparison. Apply homology; naturality of mapDerivedCategoryPlusHomologyFunctorIso for the exact forgetful functor gives a commuting square of abelian sheaves.

Apply the abelian stalk functor and compose with the inverse of Mathlib Point.sheafFiberCompIso for the coefficient forgetful functor. This functor preserves filtered colimits since it is a left adjoint. Naturality gives the required commuting square of additive maps. Convert the two stalk isomorphisms to additive equivalences. Rewrite module baseChange by the proved baseChange_eq_derivedBaseChangeMapPlus to match the original baseChangeHomologyMap.
